comments.author: @solarapparition
comments.text:
This and the “LLMs as prompt optimizers” paper make me think that non-gradient-based optimization using a frontier LLM as the optimizer might be able to solve a huge class of problems that resist numerical gradient optimization. I almost feel like this is kind of a “semantic” gradient descent, where instead of reducing loss by picking a descent direction using a mathematical gradient, you pick the descent direction based on what the LLM determines to be the direction that reduces loss.

In principle, any problem that has some numerical metric that must be optimized and has a set of optimization parameters that fit inside the context window could be susceptible to this approach.
